faqs.a: It depends on the industry: 5-10% is typical for retail, 15-20% is healthy for many small businesses, and software often exceeds 50%. Compare against your own industry, not a universal number.
faqs.q: What is a good profit margin?

faqs.a: Your cost is higher than your revenue - you lose money on every sale. Raise the price, cut the cost, or stop selling that item.
If you divide profit by the selling price, that is margin. If you divide by cost, that is markup. Most people mean margin when they say my margin is 30%.
faqs.q: Margin vs markup - which one am I using?

faqs.a: Margin = markup / (1 + markup). So 42.86% markup = 0.4286 / 1.4286 = 30% margin. The Margin and Markup Calculator on this site does it both ways.
faqs.q: How do I convert markup to margin?

faqs.a: No. The math runs entirely in your browser.

margin-calculator.formula:
Profit = revenue - cost
Margin % = profit / revenue x 100
Markup % = profit / cost x 100
howTo: Enter your total cost for the item, order, or project.

Try a higher price to see what margin you would need for your target.
keyFacts: Profit = revenue - cost. Margin = profit / revenue x 100. Markup = profit / cost x 100.
Margin answers how much of each sale do I keep; markup answers how much do I add to cost.
A 30% margin equals a 42.9% markup - same profit, different denominator.
Healthy margins vary wildly: groceries run 1-3%, software can exceed 70%.
This is gross margin (direct cost only). Rent, salaries, and taxes come out of it next.
